issue: 'h₁sn̥tyós wíHrōs deywóybʰos priHós': wíHrōs is the vocative plural of wiHrós; a singular nominative subject wiHrós is needed (agreement with h₁sn̥tyós, priHós)
'méh₂ter somHṓy ne h₁ésesi': somHṓy is the masc./neut. dative singular; 'you (mother) will not be alone' needs the feminine nominative predicate somHéh₂
'kʷóti h₂ówih₁ h₁sénti?': h₂ówih₁ is dual with a plural verb; 'how many sheep' needs the plural h₂óweyes (answered with déḱm̥ h₂óweyes)
wéwke as the imperative 'tell' of the reduplicated aorist of *wekʷ- (no labiovelar) is the engine's convention; noted only
content: the speaker tells the shepherd's daughter 'my brother loves you' though the brother has a wife (unless the wife is that daughter); grammar fine
'n̥smé h₁entér' plural 'us' for the two brothers, where the dialogue otherwise uses dual verbs (wikṓwos, préḱsowos); dual pronoun would be expected
'mówdoysu' is the locative plural 'in joys'; the exclamation 'Joy!' would be the nominative mówdos
'wĺ̥kʷoybʰos nos h₁óyneh₂m h₂ówim gʷʰént': wĺ̥kʷoybʰos is dative/ablative plural; the subject 'a wolf' must be nominative singular wĺ̥kʷos
'wésth₂e' for 'you were wearing': -th₂e is the perfect 2sg ending; *wes- 'wear' is a middle (2sg secondary middle -th₂es); stretched form
'déh₂nu éti' for 'beyond the river': éti means 'further, also, beyond (adverb)' — stretched as a preposition
'h₃réḱs' with short e (nominative is h₃rḗǵs/h₃rēḱs) and used as possessor 'the king's' where the genitive h₃rēǵés is expected
